plants.name: Chrysanthemum × morifolium
plants.description: A classic autumn perennial with dense, layered blooms in many forms, including pompon, spider, and decorative types. Its flowering is triggered by the shortening days of autumn, and it is widely grown in gardens and for cut flowers.
plants.location: Cultivated worldwide; native to East Asia, especially China and Japan
plants.funFact: Chrysanthemums are the national flower of Japan, and the Chrysanthemum Throne is the name of the Japanese imperial seat. The Festival of Happiness celebrates them each autumn.

plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: A tall, graceful tree that covers itself in clusters of trumpet-shaped lavender-blue flowers just as the southern spring reaches its peak. Fallen blossoms carpet streets and gardens in purple.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to early summer (Southern Hemisphere, October to December)
plants.location: Native to South America; widely planted in South Africa, Australia, and Argentina
plants.funFact: In Pretoria, South Africa, thousands of jacarandas bloom each spring, earning it the nickname 'Jacaranda City'. In parts of Australia, folklore says that if a jacaranda blossom falls on your head, you will pass your exams.

plants.name: Camellia sasanqua
plants.description: An evergreen shrub that blooms in the cool months, producing fragrant, delicate single or semi-double flowers with prominent golden stamens. It is one of the earliest camellias to flower and is popular in gardens in mild climates.
plants.location: Native to Japan; cultivated in the southeastern United States, Europe, and Australia
plants.funFact: Camellia sasanqua is a relative of the tea plant (Camellia sinensis), and its seeds are pressed to produce a culinary and cosmetic oil.

plants.name: Protea cynaroides
plants.description: A striking evergreen shrub with the largest flower head of any protea, a bowl-shaped bloom of pointed bracts surrounding a central cone of tiny flowers. It thrives in the fynbos vegetation, with flowering peaking in the southern spring.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter through summer, peaking in spring (Southern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Fynbos of the Western and Eastern Cape, South Africa
plants.funFact: The king protea is South Africa's national flower, and its fire-adapted underground lignotuber allows it to resprout after bushfires.
